summary: SSE micro-freeze mid-generation when edge reorders chunks under proxy buffering
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring stalls in SSE streaming sessions: the stream pauses for 6–25 seconds mid-token emission, then resumes and completes. Problem first observed after a traffic surge on 2026-03-09. The generation on our side continues (tokens emitted in runtime), but the client observes a ‘silence’ and sometimes reconnects, which causes duplicate tokens on resume.

Impact:
- QuantaDocs (enterprise/dedicated) reported multiple customer-visible chat failures; some sessions reconnected and showed duplicated tokens, breaking UX and billing reconciliation.
- Affects long-form generation (>2k token context) over SSE and some websocket connections behind the corporate proxy path.

Initial hypothesis:
Edge/ISP/corporate proxy is coalescing or reordering HTTP/2 DATA frames under burst buffering, causing SSE chunks that contain partial tokens to be held and then delivered out-of-order or delayed. Server-side keepalive heuristics interpret the gap as transient and keep producing; client-side library sees no intermediate chunks and reports a stall.

Notes on uniqueness vs other streaming issues:
This ticket focuses on chunk reordering/coalescing in the edge/proxy path (rather than worker preemption, kv-cache evictions, or model fallback). Observability shows byte-level gaps and non-monotonic request->response offsets at the edge layer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use QuantaDocs frontend behind corporate proxy (their proxy replicates client behavior).
2) Start a long SSE chat generation using openchat-7b-v1 with streaming enabled and a context >2000 tokens.
3) Simulate burst upload (small attachments) concurrently to trigger proxy buffering and HTTP/2 multiplexing.
4) Observe the client SSE stream for 10+ seconds; in affected runs the stream will pause mid-token for 6–25s then resume.
5) Capture tcpdump / h2 frames at edge to validate out-of-order/timestamped arrivals.
logs:
tcpdump snippet: frame 1023 17:22:42.111 DATA len=4096 stream=45
frame 1024 17:22:54.345 DATA len=2048 stream=46
frame 1025 17:22:54.347 DATA len=2048 stream=45 (late)
investigation_notes: Support triage: Confirmed customer environment (dedicated) and reproduced under controlled proxy buffering using squelch proxy build used by QuantaDocs.

SRE observation: Edge process (a forked Traefik) has response coalescing feature that aggregates small DATA frames under load to optimize egress throughput; coalescing weight recently increased by config change deployed 2026-03-08.

Hypothesis validated: Packet timestamps show non-monotonic delivery of stream frames for the same HTTP/2 stream id in the proxy egress queue (causes client to experience a silence mid-token when chunks are held and then flushed out-of-order).
Serving-runtime logs show continued token generation (no worker preemption), confirming stall is in transport layer, not model execution.

Risk: If client reconnects during stall, deduplication relies on client request ids; some frontend versions do not send stable request id on reconnect, causing duplicate tokens (reported by QuantaDocs).
comments: 2026-03-10T09:12:00Z - Asha Patel (Support): Customer notified support after 4 repeated stalls this morning. Captured client browser logs and provided network pcap. Asked SRE to prioritize due to P1 SLA.

2026-03-10T10:03:21Z - Mateo Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced locally using QuantaDocs proxy config. Found coalescing parameter 'egress_agg_threshold' set to 8kb; lowering to 2kb removed the pause in our tests. Raising vendor to triage upstream patch.

2026-03-10T13:45:00Z - QuantaDocs-SRE (customer): Confirmed mitigation: setting client keepalive to 10s improved UX; they will schedule proxy patch during maintenance window. Requested guidance for preventing duplicates on reconnect.

2026-03-11T08:22:10Z - Lina Chen (Developer - sse-handler): Added option to include stable 'stream-session-id' header to SSE start events so reconnects can more safely dedupe. Will land as opt-in flag behind feature flag 'sse-stable-session-v1'.
root_cause: Edge proxy response coalescing/reordering under high multiplexing load (config change 2026-03-08) caused HTTP/2 DATA frames for the same stream to be buffered and flushed non-monotonically, producing application-visible SSE silences despite continuous model output.
workaround: Customer applied two mitigations: 1) lowered proxy egress aggregation to 2kb and 2) adjusted client keepalive to 10s. Both reduced user-visible stalls in their canary tests.
resolution_plan:
Short-term: recommend patching edge-proxy to 1.4.3 which includes fix for stream ordering under coalescing (patch PR linked). Enable 'sse-stable-session-v1' feature flag for dedicated customers to avoid duplicate tokens on reconnect.
Long-term: add automated synthetic test that simulates HTTP/2 multiplexing + coalescing to catch regressions and add a telemetry metric to detect non-monotonic frame timestamps at egress.
resolution_status: Partial Mitigation - awaiting edge-proxy vendor patch and customer scheduled maintenance to upgrade. Feature-flag for dedupe scheduled in sprint 26.
follow_up_actions: Upgrade edge-proxy in prod us-east to 1.4.3 (SRE action) - target 2026-03-16 maintenance window
Roll out 'sse-stable-session-v1' flag for dedicated accounts - engineering rollout plan in PR#832
Create synthetic workload test to reproduce HTTP/2 coalescing reordering - QTR goal for infra testing
Add alerting rule: detect 'gaps_detected>0 and gap_duration_ms>5000' at sse-handler and page SRE
